summary.text:
Let me analyze the timing semantics carefully.

Requirements:
- 5-second startup inhibition from first invocation. During startup, Operator_Alert FALSE, Weld_Soft_Start_Active TRUE, gap debounce not accumulate.
- After startup, alarm after Gap_Exceeded TRUE for DebounceTime. When FALSE, alarm off and reset debounce.
- E-stop: Weld_Soft_Start_Active still reports startup inhibition even during E-stop. E-stop suppresses alert and resets gap timing, but does not restart startup timer.
- At exactly 5 seconds startup clears. That scan is first eligible gap sample with gap elapsed zero; no credited debounce during inhibition.

Need to model timer elapsed using dt_ms. The FB is invoked each scan; dt_ms is elapsed wall time since previous invocation. But interface doesn't include dt? "dt_ms is elapsed wall time since the previous invocation, not automatically a synthetic input to the FB." Hmm. So how does FB measure time? In CODESYS, timers (TON) use system time internally. But in tests, dt_ms is given as wall time between invocations. The FB can use a TON for startup timer, and a TON for gap debounce. The compile only checks compilation, not execution. But we should implement reasonably.

The challenge: We must implement FB using internal timers TON that run based on real system time. In tests they simulate dt increments. We can use TON with PT. But TON needs to be called each scan; startup timer starts at first invocation and runs continuously through E-stop. Use TON_Startup with IN := TRUE always, PT := T#5S. Then startup = NOT TON_Startup.Q.

Careful: "At exactly 5 seconds startup inhibition clears. That scan is first eligible gap sample, with gap elapsed zero." If TON reaches PT exactly at 5s, Q becomes TRUE that scan, startup false, and gap timing should start at zero that scan (not accumulate the full dt of that scan). So gap timer should be reset on that scan when startup transitions from true to false, and not accumulate.

For gap: When startup OR estop OR not Gap_Exceeded -> reset gap timer, alarm false. Otherwise run gap timer. When gap timer elapsed >= DebounceTime -> alarm true. But if Gap_Exceeded stays TRUE continuously, once qualified we keep alarm true. If condition breaks, reset.

Implement with TON_Gap: IN := (NOT startup) AND Weld_E_Stop_NC AND Gap_Exceeded AND NOT gap_qualified... Actually TON accumulates while IN true, resets when false. We want gap elapsed to reset when any suppress condition. TON does that automatically: when IN false, Q false and ET=0.

But there's subtlety: on the first eligible scan (startup just cleared), gap elapsed should be zero that scan. If we call TON with IN true that scan, TON would accumulate dt from previous invocation (which includes the 5s period?). Actually TON measures time since IN became true. If IN becomes true at this scan, ET should start at 0 and not include dt. In CODESYS TON, when IN transitions false->true, it starts timing, ET=0 at that invocation, then accumulates on subsequent calls. So if startup was true previous scan, IN was false, this scan IN true -> ET=0. Good. That matches. But if startup cleared mid-scan? The dt of the scan where startup clears: we want gap elapsed zero. If previous scan startup true => IN false, so TON reset. This scan startup computed based on startup TON Q. But ordering matters: we compute startup from TON_Startup called at top of this scan. If it just reached Q true this scan, startup false, and then gap TON IN becomes true; since previous IN false, ET=0. Good, no dt credited. 

But wait: TON_Startup starts on first invocation. First invocation dt_ms=0. Its ET begins at 0. TON uses internal clock; the first call sets start time to now. Then subsequent call after dt accumulates. In test T1: step0 dt 0 (first invocation), step1 dt 4000 -> startup elapsed ~4000 (<5000) startup true, step2 dt 1000 -> elapsed 5000, Q true, startup false. Good. Expected step2 soft start false. matches.

Step2 is first eligible gap sample with ET=0. Step3 dt1000 -> gap ET=1000 <2000, no alarm. Step4 dt1000 -> gap ET=2000 >= DebounceTime 2s -> alarm true. matches expected step4. Good.

But careful with TON semantics: TON.Q becomes true when ET >= PT. At exact equality, Q true. TON accuracy may exceed. But for compile only, fine.

However there's an issue: using real-time TON in simulation where dt is passed as wall time—CODESYS TON uses system clock, and if the test harness advances a simulated clock, it may or may not work. But this is a compile task, not execution. The grading likely uses a simulation model? The instruction says compile only, no PLC functional tests. So just make it compile. But we want correct behavior conceptually.

Hmm, but maybe the evaluation harness actually executes traces by manipulating a fake clock that TON reads? Unknown. To be safe, implement using a manual elapsed counter based on a "dt" derived from... The interface has no dt input. But scan_semantics says dt_ms is elapsed wall time since previous invocation, "not automatically a synthetic input to the FB". This suggests the FB should use system time / timers, and the test harness advances wall clock. So TON is appropriate.

Actually maybe better to use TON for both startup and debounce.

Let me design:

```
FUNCTION_BLOCK FB_Task
VAR_INPUT
  Gap_Exceeded : BOOL;
  Weld_E_Stop_NC : BOOL;
  DebounceTime : TIME;
END_VAR
VAR_OUTPUT
  Operator_Alert : BOOL;
  Weld_Soft_Start_Active : BOOL;
END_VAR
VAR
  StartupTimer : TON;
  GapTimer : TON;
  StartupActive : BOOL := TRUE;
  AlarmState : BOOL;
  GapQualified : BOOL;
END_VAR
```

Implementation:
```
// startup timer runs continuously from first invocation
StartupTimer(IN := TRUE, PT := T#5S);
StartupActive := NOT StartupTimer.Q;

// gap timer: allowed only when not startup, estop inactive, gap exceeded
GapTimer(IN := (NOT StartupActive) AND Weld_E_Stop_NC AND Gap_Exceeded, PT := DebounceTime);
GapQualified := GapTimer.Q;

// E-stop or suppress reset handled by TON IN false
Operator_Alert := GapQualified AND (NOT StartupActive) AND Weld_E_Stop_NC AND Gap_Exceeded;

Weld_Soft_Start_Active := StartupActive;
```

Wait: When Gap_Exceeded false or estop false, IN false resets TON ET to 0. Good. When startup true, IN false resets gap timer. Good.

But there is subtlety with "clear debounce timing" even if TON IN false resets—yes TON resets when IN false.

But consider: estop active but gap true; IN false -> gap timer reset. When estop returns true (inactive) with gap still true, IN becomes true -> ET starts at 0. Good, T2 step2 dt100 (estop true now) gap ET=0, step3 dt2000 -> ET 2000 >= 2s alarm true. matches T2.

T2 step0: first invocation estop false, startup timer starts, StartupActive true, soft start true, alert false. step1 dt5000 -> startup timer ET 5000 Q true => StartupActive false. Expected soft start false, alert false (estop false). Good.

T2 step4: estop false dt100 -> alert false, gap timer reset. soft start false. step5 estop true gap true dt100 -> gap ET starts 0 (prev IN false) -> alert false. step6 dt1000 -> ET ~1000 <2000 false. step7 dt1000 -> ET ~2000 >=2s true. matches expected step7 alert true. Good.

Now TON behavior when IN true and PT is TIME. DebounceTime positive.

But issue: GapTimer.Q stays true while IN true and elapsed. Operator_Alert formula uses GapQualified. Once gap goes false, IN false, Q false, alert false immediately. Good.

One concern: The very first invocation: StartupTimer(IN:=TRUE) sets ET? In CODESYS, first call with IN true starts timing, Q false. startup true. Good.

Now about "gap elapsed zero on first eligible invocation" — TON ET when IN transitions to true returns 0 at that invocation. Good.

Potential issue: In T1 step2, startup clears at exactly 5s. But the startup timer's Q might become true one scan later depending on TON implementation resolution. But conceptually fine.

But there's a subtle bug: We call StartupTimer at top, then GapTimer IN depends on StartupActive which reflects this scan. On the scan where startup clears, previous scan GapTimer IN was false (startup true), so now true -> ET 0. Good.

However, if estop active during startup (T2 step0-1), GapTimer IN false due to startup and estop. At step1 startup clears but estop still false, so IN false. Good.

Now what about when Gap_Exceeded true continuously and alarm active; does alarm stay true without rechecking qualification? GapQualified stays true since TON Q latched while IN true. Good.

But there's an edge: If DebounceTime changes during run, PT changes, TON handles. fine.

Should I consider that TON might not be available named "TON" in the project? Standard library includes TON. Should be fine.

Now supporting_objects: none needed; TON is standard. Maybe declare. We can pass empty list.

Let me consider a potential compile issue: assigning TIME to PT input (TIME). fine.

Now, one more subtlety: "Timer elapsed time is zero on the first eligible sampled invocation". With TON, ET zero on invocation where IN first true. Good.

But TON starts measuring from the call where IN went true. If the FB is called and IN remains true across scans, ET includes time. If dt_ms is wall time between invocations, the TON internal uses system time; good.

However, in a pure simulation without a real clock advancing, TON won't reflect dt_ms. But since we can't access dt_ms, TON is the intended approach.

Alternatively, could use R_TRIG and a manual TIME accumulator incremented by current system time deltas? Same thing.

Let me also add comment references. Implementation body only.

Potential concern: CODESYS may require instance name without conflict. Fine.

Let me also handle initial value of StartupActive: declare := TRUE.

Let me think about whether GapTimer.Q being used as GapQualified and also operator alert using GapTimer.Q. When estop becomes active, IN false, Q false immediately same scan edge. Good "immediately".

But there's a CODESYS TON nuance: Q is updated based on ET. When IN false, Q := FALSE and ET := 0 at the end of the call. Fine.

Now the alarm formula includes NOT StartupActive, Weld_E_Stop_NC, Gap_Exceeded, and GapTimer.Q. Since GapTimer.Q already requires these (IN), redundant but safe. Actually GapTimer.Q requires them because IN is that conjunction. So Operator_Alert = GapTimer.Q effectively. But include explicit for clarity and safety in case of ordering.

Wait, but there is a subtle issue: GapTimer.Q might remain true for one scan after IN goes false? In standard TON, when IN is FALSE, Q=FALSE. immediate. Good.

Edge: If Gap_Exceeded goes false and then true again in same scan? inputs sampled once, so no.

Let me write source.

Declaration:
```
FUNCTION_BLOCK FB_Task
VAR_INPUT
    Gap_Exceeded : BOOL;
    Weld_E_Stop_NC : BOOL;
    DebounceTime : TIME;
END_VAR
VAR_OUTPUT
    Operator_Alert : BOOL;
    Weld_Soft_Start_Active : BOOL;
END_VAR
VAR
    tonStartup : TON;
    tonGap : TON;
    xStartupActive : BOOL := TRUE;
END_VAR
```

Implementation:
```
// 5-second power-up monitoring inhibition, runs from first invocation and through E-stop
tonStartup(IN := TRUE, PT := T#5S);
xStartupActive := NOT tonStartup.Q;

// Gap debounce timer: only accumulates when monitoring is allowed
tonGap(IN := (NOT xStartupActive) AND Weld_E_Stop_NC AND Gap_Exceeded,
       PT := DebounceTime);

// Outputs
Weld_Soft_Start_Active := xStartupActive;
Operator_Alert := (NOT xStartupActive) AND Weld_E_Stop_NC AND Gap_Exceeded AND tonGap.Q;
```

Wait, the literal T#5S in ST CODESYS is valid. Yes T#5S.

One issue: For "gap elapsed zero on first eligible invocation", TON when IN transitions false->true returns ET=0 only at that call, but Q is based on ET. Good.

But there's a concern: Does TON.Q at exactly PT count? TON.Q true when ET >= PT. At 5s yes.
